barriers.description: Inherent limitations of the EHR prevented some physician feedback from being implemented in the final CDS tools, constraining designers' ability to realize proposed changes.
barriers.justification: This technical/organizational constraint impeded the designers' ability to integrate feedback and iterate the prototypes and limited their capacity to produce final design solutions that matched user recommendations.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Additionally, inherent EHR limitations prevented some physician feedback from being implemented in the final CDS tools that were deployed in the EHR.

barriers.description: Interviews were limited to physicians, so designers lacked input from other clinician roles (nurse practitioners, physician assistants, residents) that may have differing workflows and needs.
barriers.justification: This sampling limitation reduced the designers' ability to manage user understanding and to specify user requirements across all relevant user groups and contexts of use.
barriers.reference_excerpt: A limitation of our study is that interviews were limited to physicians; the input of nurse practitioners, physician assistants, and residents in training may have relevance for clinical implementation of CDS tools in differing clinical workﬂows.
